checks.body: GBIF holds 89 occurrence records for Cupriavidus necator A, concentrated in CN, IN, US. In the Rhine-Main agricultural belt, Germany GBIF holds 18 records; the 10 most-recorded non-Aves species are listed. No population parameters were declared, so whether this design could establish against what is there has NOT been evaluated. That question needs numbers no occurrence database contains.

recorded_range.reading: GBIF holds 89 occurrence records for Cupriavidus necator A, concentrated in CN, IN, US.
recorded_range.caveat: Occurrence records are presence and collector effort. They are heavily biased toward wealthy countries, roadsides, protected areas and charismatic taxa. A blank map is a map of where nobody looked as often as it is a map of where the organism is not.

numbers.relationships_note: Grouped from GloBI's own interaction types. 0 taxa recorded eating this clade, 0 recorded parasitising it, 0 in a recorded mutualistic or symbiotic relationship with it, 0 it is recorded hosting. COMPETITION IS NOT AMONG THEM, and that is not an oversight: competition is the one ecological relationship that leaves almost no direct observational trace, because it is two organisms NOT doing something to each other. GloBI records interactions that somebody watched happen. Nobody watches an exclusion. Types this grouping does not recognise, left in "other": hasVector.

how abundant anything is: occurrence counts are records, which is sampling effort as much as biology

anything about the places nobody has surveyed, which is most places
anything about Aves, which is filtered out of every result here by design and is a central part of most terrestrial communities

checks.body: Against resident soil autotroph guild, the design CANNOT invade when rare: at the resident's carrying capacity its per-capita growth rate is negative. It is excluded, on these parameters.

invader K.source: DESIGN INPUT: cells per gram of soil the designed strain is assumed to reach alone. An estimate by the designer, not a measurement; soil carrying capacities for a specific strain are not in GBIF or GloBI and were not looked up.

resident K.source: DESIGN INPUT: the standing community assumed an order of magnitude denser, on the reasoning that it is already there and adapted. An estimate, not a measurement.

alpha, resident on invader.source: DESIGN INPUT: residents assumed to suppress the invader almost as strongly as the invader suppresses itself, because they compete for the same inorganic carbon and the same electron donors.

alpha, invader on resident.source: DESIGN INPUT: the invader assumed to suppress residents weakly, being rare and novel.

numbers.model_caveat: Lotka-Volterra two-species competition: phenomenological, no space, no age structure, no environmental variation, no evolution, no third species, and one competition coefficient standing for every way two organisms can get in each other's way. The outcome above is a property of the four numbers that were declared. It is as good as they are and no better, and every one of them is an input to this result rather than an output of it.

mass_kg.source: DESIGN INPUT: smaller again once division outpaces synthesis. Stated, not measured, and the direction matters more than the number: this track does not only go up.

body_density_kg_m3.source: DESIGN INPUT: slightly denser than water, as cells generally are. Stated, not measured.

The molecular rungs are LITERATURE in Cupriavidus necator H16, Ralstonia eutropha H16 (the same strain under its former name), Escherichia coli (host for the PhaR reporter assays in link l10), each link graded and quoted. Unusually for this project the evidence IS the designed organism's own species - every link but one comes from C. necator / R. eutropha H16 itself - but it is the wild type or a metabolically engineered H16, never the designed construct, and the PhaR binding and reporter assays in l10 were run with purified protein and in E. coli rather than in C. necator.

5 law chips are out of scope for this organism: the law is about the right quantity and its numbers belong to another clade.

THE ONTOLOGY BARELY PLACES THIS BODY IN THIS ORGANISM. Of 10 parts the blueprint returned, 0 have an in_taxon restriction specific enough to be evidence that Cupriavidus necator has them; 0 are restricted only to a clade containing most of the animal kingdom, and 10 carry no restriction at all. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, so most of what is drawn here is unevidenced rather than wrong.
No part in this view has measured geometry. Every position is a declared slot in sim-engine/scales/body-frames.json, and a shape is a primitive, not a morphology.

taxon_audit.headline: Of 10 parts: 0 placed specifically, 0 placed only vacuously, 10 unconstrained, 0 contested, 0 forbidden. Only the first number is evidence that a part belongs in Cupriavidus necator.
taxon_audit.what_it_shows: Taxon constraints cannot do the work the blueprint layer asks of them. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, and for the great majority of parts the ontology either says nothing at all or says only that the part occurs somewhere in a clade containing most of the animal kingdom. That is why a fruit fly came back with bone marrow and a preen gland and without a brain: nothing in the pipeline was ever in a position to object.

verdicts.unconstrained: no in_taxon restriction exists, so the ontology is silent; not a defect and not a licence

4.what_it_taught: On the designer's own four numbers the strain cannot invade when rare: at the resident guild's carrying capacity its per-capita growth rate is negative, so it is excluded. That outcome is a property of those four numbers and not a measurement of anything, and the run says so twice. What the real databases contribute is the other half: where the clade is actually recorded, what is actually in the chosen box, and what is actually recorded as interacting with it -- facts with studies behind them, and no population parameter anywhere among them.

thompson1917-ch03-07.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth

altitude-coupling.label: Demand rises and supply falls with height together, so the flyable heights reach down to the ground
altitude-coupling.about: that the feasible set is downward closed in altitude: feasible high implies feasible low

physiology-q10.label: Q10 temperature scaling: the ratio between two temperatures is Q10 raised to their difference over ten
physiology-q10.about: how a rate changes with a ten-degree change in temperature
physiology-q10.how: Proved, no instance: no candidate commits a Q10 and the conditions file fixes 25 C. Every rate in every run is therefore at one temperature, and a design whose selling point is a rate should say which temperature it means.

genotype-developmental-ordering.label: No structure develops from a precursor that appears later than it does
genotype-developmental-ordering.about: that a claimed developmental ordering has no cycle and respects the dependencies declared for it
genotype-developmental-ordering.how: The only law in the set that is about TIME, which makes it the one the time-lapse rests on. It certifies that an ordering is consistent; it does not supply one, does not predict a rate, and says nothing about how long a stage takes. A developmental animation is therefore a declared ordering being checked for consistency, never a simulation of development.

E2.label: The fitted mass exponent lies in [2.90, 3.02]
E2.about: a measured band for the weight ratio
E2.how: A measured band from one species. Outside that species it is a number, not a constraint.

E7.label: A lever lethal before the scoring stage cannot produce the phenotype
E7.about: that a trait appearing after a lethal stage cannot be scored
E7.how: The other law about time, and the one that matters most for a time-lapse: a part that appears after the organism would have died is not a part. Pairs with the developmental ordering law.

The verifier is permitted to downgrade but not to rewrite the relation, so the sign error is recorded here and in the verification block: the "inhibits" edge to phaP3 should be split out and reversed by the owning thread.

missing_rungs.why: Cupriavidus necator is a unicellular bacterium, so there is no cell-cell interaction rung for a single planktonic cell, and nothing fetched in this run measured a cell-cell interaction in C. necator bearing on carbon fixation or swimming. The one adjacent paper found (PMC13571940, biofilm determinants in C. necator) attributes its motility and biofilm effects to genes characterised in OTHER genera (Pseudomonas, Vibrio, Aeromonas, Salmonella), so it was not used as evidence.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A C. necator transposon or deletion screen scoring aggregation, biofilm or co-culture phenotypes in this organism directly, instead of importing phenotypes from other genera.

missing_rungs.why: THE TISSUE RUNG DOES NOT EXIST FOR THIS ORGANISM. A bacterium has no tissue. This is a correct finding, not a search failure: no amount of fetching will produce it, and any tissue node in a C. necator design map would be invented.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Nothing. The ladder for a bacterium terminates at cell component and cell level, and the tissue rung should be recorded as not-applicable rather than left blank.

missing_rungs.why: THE ORGAN RUNG ALSO DOES NOT EXIST, so there is no body part for a viewer to click. The only clickable physical structures this ladder grounds are two cell components, GO_0070088 the polyhydroxyalkanoate granule and GO_0009288 the bacterial-type flagellum, plus GO_0005737 cytoplasm.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Nothing. For this organism a 3D view must be a single cell with sub-cellular compartments, not an anatomy.

missing_rungs.why: THE SWIMMING PHENOTYPE IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Nothing fetched in this run measures swimming, motility or chemotaxis in C. necator or R. eutropha. The chain reaches GO_0009288 bacterial-type flagellum (l16) and stops there: FlhDC promoter binding (l14) is in vitro, flagellar assembly (l15) is a KEGG annotation, and the only observation of the flagellum itself (l16, l17) is 2008 proteomics plus EM, with no soft-agar, tracking or chemotaxis assay. The design's swimming requirement therefore has NO measured phenotype in this organism in anything fetched here.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A soft-agar swim-plate or single-cell tracking assay on H16 wild type versus a fliC or flhDC deletion, under the autotrophic gas condition the design assumes, plus a chemotaxis assay against a defined attractant. Until that exists, any claim that the designed organism swims should be marked unverified.

missing_rungs.why: NO CARBON YIELD NUMBER WAS FOUND. The run's mass balance closes at 55%, but nothing fetched here reports a carbon or mass yield for CO2 to biomass in C. necator that could check it. The quantities found are a 13C enrichment (2.22% versus 1.13%, heterotrophic, Shimizu 2013), a dry-weight ceiling (up to 90%, review statement, Santolin 2024), and relative improvements (11% biomass, 28% PHB, Kim 2022). None of these is a yield.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A closed carbon and electron balance from a gas fermentation: gCDW and gPHB per mol CO2 consumed, with H2 and O2 uptake measured under defined autotrophic conditions. Until then the 55% figure rests on the model, not on literature.

missing_rungs.why: THE INORGANIC-CARBON UPTAKE STEP IS WEAKLY GROUNDED. Deleting the beta-carbonic anhydrase can blocks growth at ambient CO2 (l01), but the same paper concludes its primary role is anaplerotic rather than feeding RuBisCO, and no carboxysome and no native bicarbonate transporter of C. necator was identified in anything fetched here. So 'how inorganic carbon actually reaches RuBisCO' is unanswered - which matters, because this is the first step of the requirement.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Measurement of intracellular dissolved inorganic carbon and of CO2/HCO3- flux to RuBisCO in H16, plus a transporter deletion with a carbon-fixation readout rather than a growth readout.

missing_rungs.why: THE GRANULE-REGULATION RUNG IS UNSUPPORTED (break found by adversarial verification 2026-11-03, not previously recorded). The only molecule -> cell link in this ladder is l09 (PhaP1 sets the granule's surface-to-volume ratio), and the only regulator link above it is l10 (PhaR -> phaP1). Both have now been downgraded to hypothesis: l09 quotes an abstract background sentence restating an unfetched reference, and l10's EMSA is on phaP3 rather than phaP1 and reports activation, not the repression the link asserts. So nothing fetched in this run experimentally connects any single protein to the granule as a structure. The carbon chain still walks, but only through the phaCAB operon deletion (l07/l08): granule MORPHOLOGY and its regulation are ungrounded.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A phaP1 deletion and a phaP1 overexpression strain of C. necator H16 with granule number and size scored by microscopy in the fetched document itself, plus an EMSA or reporter assay on the phaP1 promoter (not phaP3) to establish the direction of PhaR control of phaP1.

method.quote_matching: Each link's quote was normalised (HTML entity unescape, unicode dash/quote/space folding, whitespace collapse) and searched as a substring in five normalisations of the file named in quote_from: raw bytes, XML tags stripped, XML tags replaced by a space, JSON string unescaping, and finally a whitespace-insensitive pass. downgraded.why: Quote is an abstract background sentence restating an unfetched reference (its ref 39); the fetched paper contains no phaP1 loss- or gain-of-function experiment. A knockout would be necessity; a statement not shown in the paper is hypothesis.

The EMSA quoted is on phaP3 binding sites, not on the link's target phaP1 (Methods name only PphaP3 fragments), and the paper's reporter assays conclude PhaR ACTIVATES phaP3 - the opposite sign to this link's relation "inhibits". No phaP1 binding or reporter experiment is in the document.

checks.body: Carbon leaving exceeds carbon entering at every corner of the stated ranges: 1.20e-14-1.20e-14 mol C/day out against 1e-14 mol C/day in. That is not an optimistic design, it is an impossible one -- the shortfall has to come from somewhere, and there is nowhere.

numbers.model: Conservation of mass on the carbon: uptake >= biomass + respired.
numbers.model_caveat: A steady-state balance over one day on ONE element. It says nothing about the energy budget, which is where carbon fixation is actually expensive -- the Calvin cycle costs ATP and reducing equivalents, and an organism can be in carbon balance and nowhere near energy balance. It says nothing about nitrogen, phosphorus or any other limiting element, nothing about whether the uptake rate is achievable by any transporter, and nothing about rate: a balance that holds per day may be unreachable per second.

checks.body: The carbon adds up at every corner: 1e-14 mol C/day in against 9.50e-15-9.50e-15 mol C/day out, a biomass yield of 0.55-0.55 mol C per mol C taken up. The correction is the loop doing its job: the first set of numbers was not pessimistic or optimistic, it was impossible, and the check said which atoms were missing rather than scoring the design badly.

taxon_audit.headline: Of 10 parts: 0 placed specifically, 0 placed only vacuously, 10 unconstrained, 0 contested, 0 forbidden. Only the first number is evidence that a part belongs in Cupriavidus necator.
taxon_audit.what_it_shows: Taxon constraints cannot do the work the blueprint layer asks of them. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, and for the great majority of parts the ontology either says nothing at all or says only that the part occurs somewhere in a clade containing most of the animal kingdom. That is why a fruit fly came back with bone marrow and a preen gland and without a brain: nothing in the pipeline was ever in a position to object.

verdicts.placed-vacuously: the only in_taxon restriction is to a clade in the top third of this organism lineage -- true of it and of most animals, so it discriminates nothing

5.what_it_taught: The request is answerable at last. The first numbers the designer proposed claimed more carbon leaving as biomass and CO2 than entered, which conservation of mass forbids outright -- and the check said impossible rather than unlikely. Corrected, the balance holds at a 55 percent yield. What the check still cannot say is everything about whether the organism could do it: no transporter kinetics, no energy budget, and carbon fixation is expensive in ATP rather than in carbon.

chain.requirement: The designed organism must take up inorganic carbon (CO2/HCO3-) and put it into biomass while also swimming; this ladder asks which enzymes and which pathway actually carry the carbon, and which cell structure carries the swimming.
chain.species_caveat: Unusually for this project the evidence IS the designed organism's own species - every link but one comes from C. necator / R. eutropha H16 itself - but it is the wild type or a metabolically engineered H16, never the designed construct, and the PhaR binding and reporter assays in l10 were run with purified protein and in E. coli rather than in C. necator.

The quote ("Electrophoretic mobility shift assays confirmed PhaR binding to all three sites.") verifies byte-for-byte, but in Cornehl 2025 those three sites are all in phaP3, not phaP1: the Methods name only PphaP3 fragments (BS1/BS2/BS3, phaP3) and the results heading reads "PhaR binds phaP3 gene at three binding sites". So (a) for the asserted target phaP1 this document shows no binding and no reporter assay - PhaR repression of phaP1 appears only as cited background - and (b) for phaP3 the paper shows the OPPOSITE SIGN to this link's relation "inhibits": its reporter assays conclude "PhaR is a transcriptional activator of phaP3" and "unlike its repressive effect on phaP1, PhaR activates phaP3 expression". The verifier is permitted to downgrade but not to rewrite the relation, so the sign error is recorded here and in the verification block: the "inhibits" edge to phaP3 should be split out and reversed by the owning thread.

missing_rungs.why: Cupriavidus necator is a unicellular bacterium, so there is no cell-cell interaction rung for a single planktonic cell, and nothing fetched in this run measured a cell-cell interaction in C. necator bearing on carbon fixation or swimming. The one adjacent paper found (PMC13571940, biofilm determinants in C. necator) attributes its motility and biofilm effects to genes characterised in OTHER genera (Pseudomonas, Vibrio, Aeromonas, Salmonella), so it was not used as evidence.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A C. necator transposon or deletion screen scoring aggregation, biofilm or co-culture phenotypes in this organism directly, instead of importing phenotypes from other genera.

missing_rungs.why: THE TISSUE RUNG DOES NOT EXIST FOR THIS ORGANISM. A bacterium has no tissue. This is a correct finding, not a search failure: no amount of fetching will produce it, and any tissue node in a C. necator design map would be invented.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Nothing. The ladder for a bacterium terminates at cell component and cell level, and the tissue rung should be recorded as not-applicable rather than left blank.

missing_rungs.why: THE ORGAN RUNG ALSO DOES NOT EXIST, so there is no body part for a viewer to click. The only clickable physical structures this ladder grounds are two cell components, GO_0070088 the polyhydroxyalkanoate granule and GO_0009288 the bacterial-type flagellum, plus GO_0005737 cytoplasm.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Nothing. For this organism a 3D view must be a single cell with sub-cellular compartments, not an anatomy.

missing_rungs.why: THE SWIMMING PHENOTYPE IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Nothing fetched in this run measures swimming, motility or chemotaxis in C. necator or R. eutropha. The chain reaches GO_0009288 bacterial-type flagellum (l16) and stops there: FlhDC promoter binding (l14) is in vitro, flagellar assembly (l15) is a KEGG annotation, and the only observation of the flagellum itself (l16, l17) is 2008 proteomics plus EM, with no soft-agar, tracking or chemotaxis assay. The design's swimming requirement therefore has NO measured phenotype in this organism in anything fetched here.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A soft-agar swim-plate or single-cell tracking assay on H16 wild type versus a fliC or flhDC deletion, under the autotrophic gas condition the design assumes, plus a chemotaxis assay against a defined attractant. Until that exists, any claim that the designed organism swims should be marked unverified.

missing_rungs.why: NO CARBON YIELD NUMBER WAS FOUND. The run's mass balance closes at 55%, but nothing fetched here reports a carbon or mass yield for CO2 to biomass in C. necator that could check it. The quantities found are a 13C enrichment (2.22% versus 1.13%, heterotrophic, Shimizu 2013), a dry-weight ceiling (up to 90%, review statement, Santolin 2024), and relative improvements (11% biomass, 28% PHB, Kim 2022). None of these is a yield.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A closed carbon and electron balance from a gas fermentation: gCDW and gPHB per mol CO2 consumed, with H2 and O2 uptake measured under defined autotrophic conditions. Until then the 55% figure rests on the model, not on literature.

missing_rungs.why: THE INORGANIC-CARBON UPTAKE STEP IS WEAKLY GROUNDED. Deleting the beta-carbonic anhydrase can blocks growth at ambient CO2 (l01), but the same paper concludes its primary role is anaplerotic rather than feeding RuBisCO, and no carboxysome and no native bicarbonate transporter of C. necator was identified in anything fetched here. So 'how inorganic carbon actually reaches RuBisCO' is unanswered - which matters, because this is the first step of the requirement.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Measurement of intracellular dissolved inorganic carbon and of CO2/HCO3- flux to RuBisCO in H16, plus a transporter deletion with a carbon-fixation readout rather than a growth readout.

missing_rungs.why: THE GRANULE-REGULATION RUNG IS UNSUPPORTED (break found by adversarial verification 2026-11-03, not previously recorded). The only molecule -> cell link in this ladder is l09 (PhaP1 sets the granule's surface-to-volume ratio), and the only regulator link above it is l10 (PhaR -> phaP1). Both have now been downgraded to hypothesis: l09 quotes an abstract background sentence restating an unfetched reference, and l10's EMSA is on phaP3 rather than phaP1 and reports activation, not the repression the link asserts. So nothing fetched in this run experimentally connects any single protein to the granule as a structure. The carbon chain still walks, but only through the phaCAB operon deletion (l07/l08): granule MORPHOLOGY and its regulation are ungrounded.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A phaP1 deletion and a phaP1 overexpression strain of C. necator H16 with granule number and size scored by microscopy in the fetched document itself, plus an EMSA or reporter assay on the phaP1 promoter (not phaP3) to establish the direction of PhaR control of phaP1.

verification.verifier: adversarial verifier, DELPHI runs thread (separate agent from the builder)
verification.stance: disbelief by default: every quote re-matched mechanically in python against the fetched bytes; nothing was fetched, and no link was added.

method.quote_matching: Each link's quote was normalised (HTML entity unescape, unicode dash/quote/space folding, whitespace collapse) and searched as a substring in five normalisations of the file named in quote_from: raw bytes, XML tags stripped, XML tags replaced by a space, JSON string unescaping, and finally a whitespace-insensitive pass. A quote spanning tag boundaries therefore still matches, but a reworded quote cannot.
method.negative_control: The matcher was proved able to fail: a planted quote ("the carbonic anhydrase was observed to cause gliding flight in the organism") inserted into a scratch copy of this file was reported FAILED, 1 of 17, while the 16 real quotes still passed.
method.fetch_log_check: Every quote_from path was looked up in runs/_chains/log/carbon-eating-bacterium.fetch.json by its saved_to field and its status read from the log, not from the filename.

downgraded.why: Quote is an abstract background sentence restating an unfetched reference (its ref 39); the fetched paper contains no phaP1 loss- or gain-of-function experiment. A knockout would be necessity; a statement not shown in the paper is hypothesis.

The EMSA quoted is on phaP3 binding sites, not on the link's target phaP1 (Methods name only PphaP3 fragments), and the paper's reporter assays conclude PhaR ACTIVATES phaP3 - the opposite sign to this link's relation "inhibits". No phaP1 binding or reporter experiment is in the document.

relation_contradiction_not_fixable_by_ve.problem: relation "inhibits" from PhaR to the phaP1-and-phaP3 node contradicts the source for phaP3, which the source shows PhaR activates. The verifier's remit allows deletion, downgrade and recording a gap, not rewriting a relation, so this is flagged rather than edited.
relation_contradiction_not_fixable_by_ve.fix_for_owning_thread: Split the node: keep PhaR -| phaP1 as hypothesis (cited background only) and add PhaR -> phaP3 as activates, grade mechanism, with the EMSA plus beta-galactosidase reporter evidence.

grades_checked_and_left_alone.l01: necessity upheld: the can deletion mutant was built in this paper (delta-RE delta-phaCAB background, deletion confirmed by clonal PCR) and the growth assay is in Figure 4C. The readout is whole-cell growth at ambient CO2 rather than carbon-fixation flux, and the paper itself notes bicarbonate is needed for the TCA cycle and nucleotide and lipid synthesis as well as the CBB cycle - which is exactly the over-attribution the molecule->pathway entry in missing_rungs already confesses, so it is not double-counted as a downgrade.
grades_checked_and_left_alone.l05: necessity upheld after reading the surrounding paragraph: Shimizu 2013 really did perform "single and double deletions of the two sets of Rubisco genes" and the 8-fold figure is wild type versus the double disruptant H16 delta-delta-cbbLS, so the deletion evidence behind the grade is in the fetched text.
grades_checked_and_left_alone.l03/l04/l07/l08/l12: necessity upheld: each quote reports an operon or gene deletion with a phenotypic readout (autotrophic growth efficiency, loss of autotrophic growth, absence of PHB granules).
grades_checked_and_left_alone.l06: association is correct and not overstated - RNA-seq fold-change only.
grades_checked_and_left_alone.l11: association upheld: a review sentence summarising gravimetric PHA content. Not raised.
grades_checked_and_left_alone.l13: sufficiency upheld: plasmid overexpression of cbbR and regA with gravimetric PHB and growth readouts is gain of function.
grades_checked_and_left_alone.l14: mechanism upheld: in vitro DNA-binding of purified cnFlhDC to the flgB and flhB promoters is a shown binding step, even though only the abstract was read.
grades_checked_and_left_alone.l02/l15: hypothesis is the honest grade for a UniProt UniRule IEA annotation and a KEGG orthology assignment; the builder did not overstate these.
grades_checked_and_left_alone.l16/l17: association upheld: 2D PAGE identification of flagellin and loss of flagella across nutrient conditions are presence and correlation, not perturbation of the flagellum.

walkability.carbon_branch: WALKS: molecule (RuBisCO cbbLS, hydrogenases hoxKGZ/hoxFUYHI, phaC1) -> pathway (GO_0019253 CBB, GO_0042619 PHB biosynthesis) -> cell (GO_0070088 PHA granule, and the whole autotrophic cell) -> phenotype (PHB as cell dry weight, 11%/28% improvement), on deletion evidence throughout (l03,l04,l05,l07,l08,l12,l11,l13).
walkability.swimming_branch: DOES NOT WALK: molecule (flhDC, fliC) -> molecule (flgB/flhB promoters, l14) -> pathway (GO_0044780 flagellar assembly, l15, KEGG annotation only) -> cell (GO_0009288 flagellum, l16, 2008 proteomics and EM, abstract only) and then STOPS. There is no phenotype rung: nothing fetched measures swimming, motility or chemotaxis in this organism. Correctly declared in missing_rungs.

cell_cell -> tissue (tissue rung does not exist for a bacterium)
tissue -> organ (organ rung does not exist for a bacterium)
cell -> phenotype for swimming (no motility assay anywhere in the run)
pathway -> phenotype for carbon yield (no yield number found)

breaks_found_newly: molecule -> cell for granule morphology and its regulation - added to missing_rungs by this verification
walkability.ungrounded_nodes_noted: l12.to (the autotrophic cell), l13.from, l13.to and l11.to carry ontology_id null, so the cell->phenotype rung of the carbon branch is real evidence hanging on nodes with no ontology id. The tissue->organ entry in missing_rungs already states that the only clickable structures are GO_0070088, GO_0009288 and GO_0005737, so this is a presentation limit rather than an undeclared break.
walkability.no_rung_was_softened: No existing missing_rungs entry was edited, weakened or removed. The six the builder declared are honest and were all independently confirmed.

cosmetic_defects_not_edited: l11.quote stores a U+FFFD replacement character where the source has a thin space ("90<?>% of its cell dry weight"); it still matches the fetched bytes, which contain the same mojibake, so the quote is faithful to the file but the file is a lossy copy of the publisher text.
l09 and l10 carry "read": "full text" although both quotes are taken from the abstract section of that full text. Not corrected: outside the verifier's edit remit.
